relations.subject: server:log-collection-task
relations.evidence: This command is used to check the status of the log collection task that is either currently running or last completed.

notable_absence.finding: This page documents two DIFFERENT status enums at two different granularities that are never reconciled with each other: the task-level Status is <running | cancelled | completed>, but the per-node Details Status is <started | collected> - a two-value enum with no 'cancelled' counterpart at all. It's never stated what a node's Status line reads if the overall task is cancelled mid-collection on that node - a genuine gap in an otherwise precisely-specified output format (the page even gives a full worked example of the exact output text).

cross_component_finding: This page is unusually precise for the batch - it reproduces the literal CLI output format verbatim (the 'No log collection tasks were found' / 'Status: ... Details: ...' block) rather than only prose-describing it, and its EXAMPLES section shows real sample output including a node name and collectinfo zip path. This is the opposite of the terse, thin-DESCRIPTION pattern seen on rebalance-status.md/rebalance-stop.md - useful negative signal that not every 'status' sibling in this corpus is equally terse; this one earns its detail because the output format itself needs specifying. No CLI-vs-REST/UI terminology drift is visible from this page's evidence.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella, where log collection status is not exposed to customers via CLI.
